title: Python datetime Module and Date-Time Types

Choose appropriate datetime classes and methods for the datetime module and its core date-time types.
Predict the output of representative PY17.1 operations.

understand.concept: Python does not use a separate primitive date type. The datetime module provides date, time, datetime and timedelta classes for representing calendar dates, clock times, combined date-times and durations. These types make date calculations explicit and avoid treating calendar values as arbitrary strings.
understand.whyItMatters: Using the correct date-time type prevents fragile string manipulation and makes comparisons, formatting and duration calculations more reliable.
understand.analogy: Date-time values are like entries on a calendar plus the hands on a clock; a duration measures the distance between two entries.
understand.analogyLimit: Real calendars include leap years, time zones and daylight-saving transitions that a simple wall calendar analogy does not fully model.
understand.summary: Python datetime Module and Date-Time Types teaches reliable representation and manipulation of Python date-time values.

explain.narrative:
## The datetime module
Import `datetime` to work with calendar and clock values. The module contains several related classes; names such as `datetime.date` and `datetime.datetime` refer to classes inside the module.

## Four core types
- `date` stores year, month and day.
- `time` stores hour, minute, second and microsecond.
- `datetime` combines a date and a time.
- `timedelta` represents a duration between date-time values.

## Choose the right type
Use `date` for birthdays or due dates, `time` for a daily opening time, `datetime` for an event at a specific date and time, and `timedelta` for an elapsed interval. Use timezone-aware datetimes when values represent real-world instants across time zones.

examples.title: Create a calendar date
examples.code:
import datetime
meeting_day = datetime.date(2026, 11, 19)
print(meeting_day)
print(type(meeting_day).__name__)
examples.explanation: date stores a calendar day without a clock time.

examples.title: Create a clock time
examples.code:
import datetime
opening = datetime.time(9, 30, 0)
print(opening)
print(type(opening).__name__)
examples.explanation: time stores clock fields without a calendar date.

examples.title: Create a combined date and time
examples.code:
import datetime
start = datetime.datetime(2026, 11, 19, 9, 30)
print(start)
print(type(start).__name__)
examples.explanation: datetime combines date and time fields.

examples.title: Represent a duration
examples.code:
import datetime
length = datetime.timedelta(hours=2, minutes=15)
print(length)
print(type(length).__name__)
examples.explanation: timedelta represents a duration rather than a point on the calendar.

examples.title: Inspect the class names from the module
examples.code:
import datetime
print(datetime.date.__name__)
print(datetime.time.__name__)
print(datetime.datetime.__name__)
print(datetime.timedelta.__name__)
examples.explanation: The module groups related classes under one import namespace.
